source_user: Advanced cluster case NVIDIA Dynamo-112: Design an evaluation of NVIDIA Dynamo for disaggregated inference orchestration. Variant 112 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: separate frontend routing, prefill workers, decode workers, KV movement, transport overhead, scheduling policy, queueing, model compatibility, observability, and failover behavior. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer: Assumptions and scope: pin and verify the deployed NVIDIA Dynamo release, model/tokenizer, software/driver/CUDA versions, topology and GPU/NIC/RDMA configuration; declare context/output-length distributions, request mix, concurrency, offered load, batching, cache warmth, placement, tenant policy, correctness and deadline targets. Do not infer platform-specific behavior without documentation or an observed trace. Hypothesis for variant 112: under matched workload, quality, and offered load, the proposed disaggregated orchestration changes a predeclared primary metric (for example p95 TTFT, p99 end-to-end latency, or completed requests/s) by a predeclared margin while keeping p99 ITL, timeout/error rate, output correctness, isolation, and cost within predeclared limits. Use least-privilege, read-only inspection first: verify the pinned release/configuration, component readiness, model/KV compatibility, queue and scheduler state, and correlated request IDs before any change. Run only a bounded canary or fault injection with redacted outputs, explicit timeout/error/correctness/isolation rollback gates, and a tested return to the known-good route. The evaluation must distinguish measured facts from estimates and separate frontend routing, prefill, decode, KV movement, transport, scheduling, queueing, compatibility, observability, and failover effects. Define an ordinary non-disaggregated or current-production baseline with identical model, traffic, batching, placement constraints, and quality checks; report units, confidence intervals or other uncertainty, and negative results. Failure/rollback condition: stop the canary and restore the known-good configuration if any predeclared SLO, correctness, authorization/isolation, compatibility, error/timeout, or data-integrity gate regresses; retain synchronized traces and configuration diffs for review. Evidence required before claiming improvement includes pinned inventories, raw traces and counters, repeated matched trials, ablations, fault-injection/recovery results, and rollback artifacts.
risks: Release-specific NVIDIA Dynamo behavior and supported configuration may differ; verify against the pinned deployed build.
Aggregate metrics can be confounded by workload mix, batching, cache warmth, placement, saturation, retries, topology, or instrumentation overhead.
Canaries and fault injection can affect availability, correctness, security, or tenant isolation; bound scope and preserve evidence.
evidence_required: Pinned release, model, topology, configuration, and software/driver inventory.
Synchronized raw per-request traces plus stage and RDMA counters with units.
Matched randomized baselines, ablations, strata, repeated trials, and uncertainty estimates.
Correctness, compatibility, authorization/isolation, fault-injection, rollback, and recovery artifacts.
